device.name: Flightmare vectorized quadrotor environment
device.vendor: Robotics and Perception Group, University of Zurich

facts.text: FlightEnvVec is a Stable-Baselines VecEnv for the native vector environment.
FlightEnvVec builds a per-agent observation space Box(-inf, inf) with num_obs entries and a per-agent action space Box(-1, 1) with num_acts entries.
FlightEnvVec.seed delegates to the native wrapper's setSeed method.

FlightEnvVec.step calls the native batch step and returns copied observation, reward and done arrays plus a list of per-environment info dictionaries; on a done environment it adds an episode reward/length entry and clears that environment's reward history.
FlightEnvVec.reset calls the native reset and returns a copy of the batched observations.
FlightEnvVec.num_envs delegates to the native wrapper's getNumOfEnvs method.
The native VecEnv::step requires action, observation, reward and done matrices whose rows equal num_envs and calls perAgentStep for every environment.
perAgentStep stores each environment's step reward and terminal flag, and when an environment is terminal it resets that environment and adds the terminal reward before the batch step returns.
The pybind module exposes the vector environment as flightgym.QuadrotorEnv_v1 with reset, step, setSeed, close, getNumOfEnvs, getObsDim, getActDim and getExtraInfoNames.
QuadrotorEnv::isTerminalState returns true, with terminal reward -0.02, when the position-z state is at most 0.02.
The pinned quadrotor environment configuration sets sim_dt to 0.02 s and max_t to 5.0 s; both are configuration defaults, not universal bounds.
The random generator used by the quadrotor reset is an mt19937 seeded from std::random_device at construction, so the wrapper's std::srand seed does not seed that generator.
The flightros FlightPilot subscribes to flight_pilot/state_estimate (nav_msgs/Odometry) to update a rendering quadrotor.
The flightros FlightPilot timer callback mainLoopCallback is empty; the node is not a trajectory or actuator server.

determinism.notes: the package fake seeds Python's random.Random from the supplied value; the upstream EnvBase::setSeed only calls std::srand while reset draws from an mt19937 seeded from std::random_device (env_base.hpp:39,62), so no upstream or bit-exact determinism is claimed

fidelity.engine: analytic:vector-environment fake with no flightlib physics or Unity rendering
gaps: the fake is an analytic stand-in, not a recording: it integrates a placeholder altitude and observation from the action, with no flightlib rigid-body dynamics, no quadrotor model, no contacts, no sensors and no Unity rendering
the fake uses the shipped QuadrotorEnv dimensions (12 observations, 4 actions) as placeholders; FlightEnvVec itself takes its dimensions from whatever pybind implementation it wraps
20 ms is the pinned quadrotor_env.yaml sim_dt default and is configurable; the fake does not integrate that timestep, it only counts one environment step per bridge tick
the adapter serves one environment (num_envs == 1); a larger native batch is refused rather than stepping the unselected rows with invented actions or reducing their rewards and terminations

the native VecEnv auto-resets a done environment inside the same step and returns the post-reset observation; the adapter reports terminated and, with autoreset false, the bridge refuses the next step until an explicit reset (which resets the native environment again)
the native seed path does not seed the mt19937 used by reset, so a live deployment cannot claim the seeded determinism that the fake implements for testing
a real backend needs the flightgym pybind extension built from flightlib and a configured FLIGHTMARE_PATH; neither is installed here and no live simulator or hardware run was made
the package exposes no image, point-cloud, camera or Unity render capability; only cap.world.step, cap.world.reset and cap.world.seed are bound

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulated world stops advancing: the runtime latches the e-stop and no world step, reset or seed is accepted until an explicit safety reset clears the latch; no physical actuator or hardware stop exists in this package
